name: Civic Square
reason: Civic open space whose sights (Legislative Assembly, Canberra Museum and Gallery, theatre, library) are separate candidates or civic buildings; Wikivoyage 'See' lists it as a block, nothing to do in the square itself beyond the Mount Ainslie sight line.
objection: Wikivoyage places it first in Civic's See list and notes the deliberate alignment with Mount Ainslie, so a guide singles it out as a landmark.

name: Artworld ADG
reason: Commercial Aboriginal art shop/gallery open Fri only; plain shop, not a place to visit (rule 2).
objection: Wikivoyage lists it under See with artefacts to look at, and it is free to browse.

name: Glebe Park
reason: Wikivoyage Civic names it as a pleasant stroll and an autumn-colour photo spot (one counted source); 40 ha? urban park. Case for: a guide singles it out, free, open always. Case against: an ordinary city-centre park, one source, short visit.
objection: Run rule rejects urban parks no guide singles out; Wikivoyage does single it out but only in one sentence.

name: Sydney and Melbourne buildings
reason: Heritage commercial buildings with restaurants and bars, seen from the street (loggias); exterior-only, a Wikivoyage 'See' mention but nothing to do (rule 2).
objection: Wikivoyage names them as landmarks in Civic and on the main Canberra page, and the 1920s loggias can be walked through.

name: ACT Memorial
reason: Minor war memorial on London Circuit, a plaque-scale stop (rule 3).
objection: Named in Wikivoyage See list and has its own Wikipedia article.

name: Canberra Centenary Column
reason: Minor commemorative sculpture on London Circuit, a ten-minute look with no guide singling it out beyond a one-line listing (rule 3).
objection: Wikivoyage describes it in detail with a photo, so it is a recognised public artwork.

name: Legislative Assembly Building
reason: Government building; Wikivoyage says it has educational programs by booking only, so not open to walk-in visitors; exterior/civic building (rule 2).
objection: Wikivoyage lists it with contact details and a visit can be booked; a school-programme visit is not a general visitor offer.

name: Reserve Bank of Australia Building
reason: Former bank office building seen from outside; heritage listing alone is not a visit (rule 2).
objection: Commonwealth Heritage Listed, named in Wikivoyage Civic.

name: Dendy Cinemas Canberra
reason: Commercial cinema, a business venue not a place to visit (run rule: cinemas rejected).
objection: Two counted sources (Wikivoyage, VisitCanberra) list it.

name: Palace Electric Cinemas
reason: Commercial cinema, a venue not a visitor attraction (run rule).
objection: Independent arthouse cinema with a Wikipedia article; a screening is something to do.

name: Canberra Merry-Go-Round
reason: Wikivoyage Civic lists a heritage-listed 1914 carousel (52 carved horses, mechanical organ, $3 a ride, set daily hours) in a permanent pavilion on City Walk. Case for: heritage landmark, permanent. Case against: a ride of a few minutes, one source, a short visit, an operated amusement.
objection: Rule rejects operators and rides; here the carousel is a heritage object in a fixed place, but a $3 ride is about 5 minutes.

name: Casino Canberra
reason: Commercial gaming venue (run rule: casinos rejected).
objection: Wikivoyage lists it and it has a Wikipedia article with 3k views.

name: Holey Moley Golf Club
reason: Indoor mini-golf novelty venue, a business (run rule).
objection: Two counted sources include it, so visitors do play there.

name: Kingpin Canberra
reason: Indoor bowling and arcade, a business (run rule).
objection: Listed by Wikivoyage as something to do.

name: Status Golf
reason: Golf simulator centre and bar, a business (run rule).
objection: Listed by Wikivoyage as something to do.

name: Canberra Glassworks
reason: Two counted sources (VisitCanberra museums page and attractions page; also Wikivoyage South Canberra): glassblowers work in the hot shop in the historic Kingston Power House, plus gallery; a 30+ minute visit, open to the public (rule 1,2). Opened visitcanberra museums page.
objection: It is a working studio with a gift store, and Wikivoyage's listing is marked a dead link, so hours may be unreliable.

name: Old Bus Depot Markets
reason: Weekly Sunday market, not there whenever you arrive (rule 4).
objection: About 200 stalls and VisitCanberra names it, so it is a strong draw on Sundays.

name: Haig Park Village Markets
reason: Weekly Sunday market (rule 4); the park itself is not the candidate.
objection: Two counted sources list it.

name: Little Burley Market
reason: Weekly Saturday market (rule 4).
objection: Named by VisitCanberra's 100 things list.

name: Belconnen Fresh Food Markets
reason: Weekly market with no counted source (rule 1 and 4).
objection: A food market is a real local draw.

name: Fyshwick Fresh Food Markets
reason: Weekly market, no counted source found in the candidate (rule 1 and 4); I did not confirm a daily trading market, so it is not kept as a market hall.
objection: Fyshwick Markets may trade several days a week (Thu-Sun); if a source shows that and names it, it could qualify as a market hall.

name: Canberra City Art Trail
reason: VisitCanberra museums page names a self-guided walk through the city centre passing iconic installations. Case for: a named agency walk, free, always available. Case against: one counted source, a route of scattered artworks not a single place, no list of stops in hand.
objection: A trail is a route not a spot, and the installations are individually minor.

name: Tuggeranong Art Trail
reason: VisitCanberra names a family-friendly self-guided art trail in Tuggeranong with short drives and easy walks. Case for: agency-named, free, permanent. Case against: one counted source, aimed at kids, a scattered route with no single destination.
objection: Same objection as the City Art Trail, plus weaker billing.

name: Commonwealth Place
reason: Two counted sources (Wikivoyage South Canberra, VisitCanberra attractions): lakeside public place with the International Flag Display (110 flags, open 24 hours) and lake views; a stroll of half an hour next to the National Library and Questacon (rule 1-3). Opened Wikivoyage South Canberra.
objection: A plaza and flag display is a short stop; the lake views are not unique and visitors are mainly in the Triangle for the institutions.

name: Constitution Place
reason: No counted source (only Wikipedia); a civic open space in Parkes, a minor memorial-type place (rules 1, 3).
objection: Reconciliation Place has public artworks and a Wikipedia article, so a source might exist.

name: Reconciliation Place
reason: No counted source (only Wikipedia); a commemorative open space in Parkes, a minor memorial-type place (rules 1, 3).
objection: Reconciliation Place has public artworks and a Wikipedia article, so a source might exist.

name: Magna Carta Place
reason: No counted source (only Wikipedia); a commemorative open space in Parkes, a minor memorial-type place (rules 1, 3).
objection: Reconciliation Place has public artworks and a Wikipedia article, so a source might exist.

name: Aboriginal Tent Embassy
reason: Wikivoyage Canberra names it (one counted source); a long-standing protest and cultural site on the Parliament lawns with its own history, exempted from the Anzac/lakeside memorial rule (run brief). Relied on the brief plus Wikivoyage Canberra, which mentions it.
objection: One source, an open lawn with tents and flags; the visit may be short.

name: Australian-American Memorial
reason: Wikivoyage North Canberra calls it the only sight of interest at Russell Offices (the main Canberra page names it too): a tall column visitors can walk to. Case for: a landmark visible from the lake axis, free, always open. Case against: a minor memorial, a short stop, set in a defence office area.
objection: Brief rules minor memorials out unless a source singles them out; Wikivoyage does single this one out as the only sight there.

name: King George V Memorial
reason: No counted source (Wikipedia only) and a minor memorial sculpture (rules 1, 3).
objection: A public art landmark by the lake with a Wikipedia article.

name: Kemal Atatürk Memorial
reason: part of Anzac Parade / a minor memorial: no visitor source singles it out as a visit in its own right; the avenue is the place (Wikivoyage North Canberra lists it only as one of the Anzac Parade memorials).
objection: Each is a recognised national memorial with its own Wikipedia article and Wikivoyage listing, so a visitor could spend ten minutes at it; but that is the 'minor memorial' case and Anzac Parade carries the visit.
